answer: Consider a decentralized market where a lotus contract enforces dynamic opportunity cost bonds and subgame perfect punishment matrices. Let an attacker deploy $k>1$ Sybil identities in an open ocean of agents, seeking resource capture. Because collateral lockup scales superlinearly while aggregate rewards remain bounded, the marginal yield of identity multiplication turns strictly negative.
